en: for it is my own self.
for it is a thing of mine.
Ah! Oh give me your love!
In the week when we must go [?],
we will go off to sleep.
When the little priest gives us
I will give you my little hand
and the priest two sprinkles of holy water.
at the least we will have seven,
notes: Válgame Dios, literally 'may God avail me', an exclamation: 'God help me!'.
Allá voy yo, literally 'there I go': 'I am coming', 'here I come'.
Lines 1.5 and 5.7: Guachinanga, guachinanguitos: in Cuban Spanish guachinango was a name for a Mexican, and the word is usually read so here [?].
Line 2.4: es mi persona, literally 'it is my person', i.e. it is I.
Lines 2.9 and 2.12: chinita, a term of endearment for a girl or woman, not a name.
Line 3.3: 'en la semana que hay ir' is unclear: perhaps 'in the week we have to go'.
Line 4.1: curita, 'little priest', an affectionate diminutive of cura.
Line 4.7: hisopazos, strokes of the hisopo, the aspergillum that sprinkles holy water.
